title: Temporal Recency Bias in Skill Libraries: Task-Phase-Dependent Harm to Forward-Looking Analysis in Frozen-Executor Agents
metric_summary: 96/96 valid frozen evaluation units; difficulty gate PASS (backward=0.50, forward=0.25, gap=0.25); heldout direct phase×recency harm interaction=0.000 (stage4=0.000, stage8=0.000); additive same-information baseline heldout Brier=0.134204, interaction model=0.134577, improvement=-0.000374; 2 prior valid evaluation receipts reused + 94 v5 receipts; 108 scientific provider calls total within frozen 192-call cap.
problem_text: In a frozen-executor agent with a self-evolved skill library and recency-biased retrieval, forward-looking prediction tasks will show a larger performance degradation as the library grows and recency bias increases, compared to backward-looking summarization tasks of matched difficulty. This differential harm will persist after controlling for retrieval quality (relevance scores), task difficulty (no-skill baseline accuracy), and skill-task compatibility (origin-task distribution).
strongest_reduction: A retrieval-quality + task-difficulty + skill-compatibility baseline that receives the same relevance scores, task difficulty metrics, and skill origin-task metadata, and predicts harm as a function of these variables without a recency × task-phase interaction term.
search_closure_avoid: paraphrase-only revival of the claim that recency weighting selectively harms forward-looking tasks without a new held-out same-information residual

changing backward/forward task difficulty, skill-library composition, retrieval information, executor, or evaluation task semantics and treating the resulting difference as a reopening of the frozen P12 object
retuning the phase-interaction or Brier thresholds after observing outcomes, or weakening the additive same-information baseline to manufacture a recency-specific residual
reopen_condition: Reopen this exact P12 recency-bias search basin only if a new preregistered, protocol-valid same-information study preserves matched backward/forward difficulty, the frozen skill/retrieval information boundary available to the additive baseline, task semantics, executor, and predeclared analysis thresholds, yet demonstrates a held-out phase×recency harm residual beyond that baseline: under the current contract, heldout direct interaction >=0.25, heldout Brier improvement >=0.02, and stage8 interaction >= stage4, or a stronger preregistered residual criterion fixed before outcomes. Changing task family, skill library, baseline information, evaluator, threshold, or merely renaming recency interference does not reopen this closure.
